captions.instagram:
On H-1B with a spouse on H-4 who can't get a Social Security number? You can usually still file a joint return.

✔️ Everyone on the return needs an SSN or an ITIN.
✔️ A first-time ITIN application (Form W-7) is generally attached to the front of the tax return, with a passport or certified copy.
✔️ If your spouse is a nonresident for tax, you can choose to treat them as a resident to file jointly. Then both of you report worldwide income.
✔️ An ITIN is for tax filing only. It doesn't allow work or change immigration status.

We prepare H-1B family returns, federal plus NJ and NY. Book a call to check your filing status. Not available for CT, MD or OR state returns.

Tax information only, not immigration advice.

sources.fact: A spouse must have an SSN or ITIN to be on a joint or separate return; if not eligible for an SSN, file Form W-7 for an ITIN; choice to treat a nonresident spouse as resident: both report worldwide income, signed statement with the joint return (read 2026-10-25)
Attach Form W-7 to the front of your tax return (exceptions listed); original passport or certified copy is sufficient ID (Instructions for Form W-7, read 2026-10-25)
An ITIN doesn't authorize work in the U.S. or provide/change immigration status (read 2026-10-24)
